case_text:
Vignette:
A 25-year-old woman presents with bilateral thigh soreness that began yesterday, approximately 36 hours after her first gym session involving squats and lunges. She has not exercised regularly before. The soreness is worse with movement, particularly going downstairs. She denies any acute injury, popping sensation, bruising, or swelling. She has no history of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. On examination, both quadriceps and hamstrings are mildly tender to palpation bilaterally. There is no edema, ecchymosis, warmth, or joint effusion. Range of motion of both knees and hips is full, though mildly uncomfortable at end range. She ambulates normally.
